['-abcx'] -> {a:true,b:true,c:'x'}. ['-acb'] -> {a:true,c:'b'} (b not set, since -c takes the rest of the group as its value).

['--cheese','--verbose'] -> opts {cheese:true, verbose:true}, args []. ['--cheese','-5'] -> opts {cheese:'-5'}, args [] (optional value consumes next token unless it looks like an option; negative numbers allowed) - partly a guess. ['--','--cheese'] -> opts {}, args ['--cheese'].

tests/*.test.js (fixtures in tests/fixtures). One file: node --test tests/command.hook.test.js. One case: node --test --test-name-pattern='when ...' tests/file.test.js (not in doc, guess). Tests use .exitOverride() (throws CommanderError instead of process.exit) and .configureOutput({writeErr: () => {}, writeOut: ...}) to suppress output, and parse(..., {from:'user'}).

Precedence cli > env > implied > default. Env is applied after CLI so it can check what the CLI set; _parseOptionsEnv only applies the env var if the current value is undefined or its source is default/config/env, so it never overwrites a CLI value (and env beats default/config).
